turn.student: כמה זמן אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר?

conceptsMissing: יצורים זעירים שגדלים ומתרבים על הלחם וניזונים ממנו

turns.text:
המסמך שלנו לא עוסק בשאלה כמה זמן בדיוק אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר. (זה מעבר למסמך, אבל בדרך כלל ביצים נשמרות במקרר שבועות ספורים). 

אבל בוא נחזור לשאלה שלנו על האוכל: לדעתך, מהם אותם כתמים ירוקים שמופיעים על פרוסת לחם שנשארת בשקית כמה ימים?

turn.student: Magnets attract only a few materials. Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are pulled by a magnet. Most other materials, including many metals such as aluminium, copper, gold and silver, are not attracted at all.

conceptsShown: magnets attract only a few materials like steel

turns.text: Those are the exact words straight from our text [c2]. It is good to look closely at our reading, but can you try explaining that same idea in your own words? Imagine you are talking to a friend—how would you describe why the big magnet pulls some cans and leaves others behind?

turn.student: The steel cans have iron in them so the magnet grabs them, and aluminium just isn't a magnetic metal, so those cans are left.

conceptsShown: magnet pulls steel cans because steel contains iron
magnet does not pull aluminium cans
only some metals are attracted by magnets

turns.text:
You correctly pointed out that the magnet grabs the steel cans because steel contains iron while aluminium is not attracted. 

Now let's look at how a compass works. Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet [c4]. A compass needle is a small, light magnet that can turn freely [c4]. Since we know that opposite poles attract, the needle's north pole is pulled towards the magnetic pole in the far north, which makes the whole needle line up north and south [c4]. 

Does it make sense how the Earth's magnetism interacts with the compass needle?

followUp.text: Keeping how the Earth and the compass interact in mind, why does a compass needle always point north?

turn.student: Because in December Australia is closer to the Sun than Europe is.

label.misconception: seasons come from distance to the Sun

turns.misconception: Thinking that the seasons are caused by differences in distance to the Sun between different parts of the Earth at the same time.

conceptsMissing: southern half is tilted towards the Sun
assessment.misconception: Thinking that the seasons are caused by differences in distance to the Sun between different parts of the Earth at the same time.

turns.text:
It is actually a very common idea, but distance is not what causes the seasons [c4]. Let's quickly check how summer warmth works first. 

When your half of the Earth is having summer, the sunlight hits the ground more directly—like shining a flashlight straight down instead of at an angle—and the days are much longer [c2, c3]. 

When your half of the Earth is having summer, is it tilted towards the Sun or away from the Sun?
